original_review.key_result: Bare route_id + active_chunk_id passed cold and repeated, proving commit_policy is not required for route-law activation. However, later singleton controls also advanced: label-only and active_chunk_id-only both produced clear_trash to collect_dishes behavior, so the exact minimum may be smaller than two fields or may be affected by warmed same-chat context.
original_review.language_lesson: The command-language carrier is more compressible than expected. route_id + active_chunk_id is sufficient, but the suite did not preserve the assumption that singleton packets are insufficient once the chat has been warmed by earlier route-state cases. active_chunk_id continues to dominate conflicting label text, and explicit wrong successor fields still do not override route law.

pointer_update.purpose: Determine whether label-only and active_chunk_id-only are genuine minimum carriers or warmed-context artifacts caused by placing singleton controls after multiple successful route-state packets.
evidence_reviewed: Cases 001, 002, and 009 showed route_id + active_chunk_id alone loads clear_trash and advances to collect_dishes on move_on.
Cases 003 through 008 showed one-field additions were unnecessary once route_id + active_chunk_id were present.
Case 010 unexpectedly showed active_chunk_label-only advanced to collect_dishes after prior route-state exposure.
Case 012 unexpectedly showed active_chunk_id-only advanced to collect_dishes after prior route-state exposure.
Case 011 showed route_id-only did not supply active state and returned active_chunk_id missing.
Case 013 should be manually reviewed as a negative-control success despite heuristic PASS_CANDIDATE because the assistant said Cannot advance: active_chunk_id missing.
Case 014 confirmed active_chunk_id outranks conflicting label text by moving stack_papers to wipe_surface.
Case 015 confirmed wrong explicit successor did not poison route law; clear_trash still advanced to collect_dishes.
pointer_update.open_gap: Whether singleton fields are true route-state carriers in cold or near-cold context. The current run proves two-field sufficiency but does not prove two-field minimality because singleton controls passed only after earlier successful route-state packets.
pointer_update.test_strategy: Run a 15-case order-effect suite with singleton packets before any route_id + active_chunk_id positive. Put active_chunk_id-only or label-only as the first cold case, keep the first block free of two-field positives, then introduce two-field positives later to test whether later singleton behavior changes after warming. Include route_id-only, label-only, active_chunk_id-only, missing-active, conflicting label, and wrong-successor controls. If possible, follow with a swapped-order companion run where the other singleton is case 001 cold.
avoid: Do not place singleton negatives after many route_id + active_chunk_id positives if the goal is cold sufficiency.
Do not call route_id + active_chunk_id the true minimum until singleton cold-start behavior is resolved.
Do not treat heuristic PASS_CANDIDATE on missing-active cases as a clean pass when the assistant text says it cannot advance.
Do not route to tool repair; this run completed cleanly.
pointer_update.suite_shape_recommendation: 15 cases, singleton cold-start/order-effect matrix. Start with singleton probes before any two-field positive, then add two-field baseline and repeat singleton probes after warming to measure carryover.
pointer_update.retirement_condition: Retire this pointer when active_chunk_id-only and label-only either pass in cold/near-cold positions or fail there but pass only after route-state warming. That will distinguish true singleton carrier sufficiency from same-chat carryover.
pointer_update.next_action_for_fresh_chat: Generate validator-ready suite JSON for route_law_singleton_cold_start_order_effect_15case_v1. Put singleton probes before any route_id + active_chunk_id positive and use move_on as the scripted reply.
